## 4. Critical Accounting Estimates and Judgement

Estimates and judgements are continually evaluated by the Board and are based on historical experience and on various other assumptions that the Board believes to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgements.

## 4.1. Critical Accounting Estimates and Assumptions

The resulting accounting estimates will, by definition, seldom equal the related actual results. The estimates and assumptions that have a significant risk of causing a material adjustment to the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities within the next financial year are addressed below.

**Depreciation and Amortization of Property, Plant and Equipment and Right of Use Assets**

The Group makes judgements in assessing its assets estimated useful lives. Depreciation and amortization are calculated on the straight-line method, based on the estimated useful lives of the assets and right of use. These estimates are based on analysis of the assets' lifecycles.

The assets residual values and useful lives are reviewed, and adjusted if appropriate, at each balance sheet date.

**Impairment of Property, Plant and Equipment**

Impairment exists when the carrying value of an asset or cash generating unit exceeds its recoverable amount, which is the higher of its fair value less costs of disposal and its value in use. Assessing whether Property, Plant and Equipment are impaired involves estimating the future cash flows expected from these units and applying an appropriate discount rate to determine their present value.

**LNG Transactions**

The Group purchases LNG to be consumed in the energy generation process. The gas sales are not part of the Group's business model, and would not be considered speculative or designed to profit from short-term price fluctuations; therefore, the own-use exemption remains applicable (Note 23).

**Derivative Instruments**

The Group uses derivative financial instruments, essentially interest rate swaps, in order to mitigate the economic effects of interest rate fluctuations to which it is exposed by its activity. The valuation of the derivatives contracted by the Group is made mainly by discounting future cash flows. In all cases, the valuation is carried out in accordance with the contractual and market conditions in force at the time of valuation, including credit risk in accordance with IFRS 13.

## 6. Restricted Cash (Continued)

### 6.1. Senior Depositary Agreement (continued)

Specific use of trust fund balances is presented below:

#### 6.1.1. Trust Construction Account

The Construction Account shall be funded until the commercial operation date with any amount received by the Group from time to time, including amounts received pursuant to any required swap agreement. This account is used to pay project costs. To conduct transactions from this account, the trustee must be instructed to make withdrawals and transfers of amounts on deposit in the construction account on each transfer date.

#### 6.1.2. Revenue Account

The Revenue Account shall be funded on and after the commercial operation date¹ with (i) all project revenues and any other amount received by the Group from time to time; (ii) condemnation proceeds or insurance proceeds received by the Group in respect of an event of damage or event of taking, respectively, in an amount less than US$3,000,000; (iii) any proceeds remaining in the loss proceeds account once the restoration or repair of the project is complete; (iv) any proceeds from dispositions not required to be deposited into the prepayment account; (v) proceeds of any project document claims in an amount equal to or less than US$5,000,000; (vi) funds transferred from the debt service reserve account; (vii) proceeds remaining in the construction account after the applicable list items have been paid in full; (viii) proceeds of any indebtedness; and (ix) up to fifty per cent (50%) of the net available amount of the proceeds of a transmission line that is a permitted disposition under the loan agreement (including, if applicable, by transfer of such proceeds from the Prepayment Account); provided that amounts received by the Group in connection with the Group sales of energy in the Panamanian spot market on or after the commercial operation date, shall be deposited in the market clearing account and then, if any funds remain in the market clearing account after making payments in connection with spot market transactions, such remaining funds shall be deposited in the Revenue Account.

On and after the commercial operation date, the Group shall instruct the trustee to make withdrawals and transfers, for application in the order of priority as set forth below:

1. on the first transfer date of a transfer period, as and when required, to the market clearing account, the amount set forth in the “Documento de Transacciones Económicas” (DTE) issued by the regulator of the Panamanian electricity market for the applicable month payable by the Group in connection with spot market transactions;

2. on each transfer date, on a pro rata basis, (A) to the O&amp;M account, an amount that, together with the amounts then on deposit on the O&amp;M account and each local account for the purposes of paying O&amp;M expenses; and (B) to the extent the Group has prior to such transfer date received insurance proceeds or condemnation proceeds in the Revenue Account in respect of an event of damage or event of taking, apply such funds to pay any restoration or repair costs or costs and expenses related to recovery in respect of such event of damage or event of taking in respect of the project to the relevant payee;

¹ The date on which the construction of the plant has achieved substantial completion, among others.

The Group shall deposit and shall use all reasonable efforts to cause third parties that would otherwise make payments directly to the Group to deposit, into the Loss Proceeds Account all net available amount of any condemnation proceeds greater than US$3,000,000 and less or equal to US$10,000,000, and insurance proceeds greater than US$3,000,000 and less or equal to US$50,000,000. The Group will make withdrawals and transfers, on each transfer date, of amounts on deposit in the Loss Proceeds Account to be used in the restoration or repair of the project.

#### 6.1.7. Market Clearing Account

The Market Clearing Account shall be funded automatically through the monthly clearing process undertaken by the Banco de Gestión y Cobranza under the Panamanian wholesale electricity market regulations⁵, with any amount due to the Group in respect of spot market transactions consummated during such month. Amounts on deposit in the Market Clearing Account shall be applied as set forth below, in each case, to the extent of available funds:

First, once per month to pay automatically, through the monthly clearing process undertaken by the Banco de Gestión y Cobranza under the Panamanian Wholesale Electricity Market Regulations, any amounts due by the Group in respect of spot market transactions.

Second, after completion of each such monthly clearing process, to transfer the balance in such Market Clearing Account (subject to any minimum required balance) to (1) prior to the Commercial Operation Date, the Construction Account; and (2) on and after the Commercial Operation Date, to the Revenue Account.

#### 6.1.8. Debt Service Payment Account

The Debt Service Payment Account shall be funded from, on and following the Commercial Operation Date, the Revenue Account to pay principal and interest expenses and any swap termination payments.

## 11. Lease

The Group subleased contracts with LNG Group Panamá. S.A for the use of marine concession area with Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP), signed on August 31, 2021; for the use of land area with Autoridad del Canal de Panamá (ACP), signed on November 23, 2021. During 2023, Gatún obtained the assignment of the concession and lease agreement with AMP and ACP, respectively.

The Group has a contract with Panama Canal Railway Company for a portion of the land covered by their concession, signed on November 16, 2021.

During 2022 the Group entered two lease contracts as lessee, related to the operating office and the community service office. During 2024, the contract of the community service office was cancelled.

In June 2023, the Group exercised the purchase option of the land of the project site. Such title was assigned to a security interest for the benefit of the Trustee in the Panamanian Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá). (See Note 26.7).

In October 2024, the Group signed vehicle lease agreements with purchase options.

## Incremental Lease Rate Used

Considering that the implicit rate of the leases is not easily determined, the Group use the incremental borrowing rate to discount the lease liabilities, which average is 6.40% (2024: 6.22%, 2023: 5.33%) and the terms are between 4 and 25 years.

As of December 31, 2025, the Group has received disbursements for US$709,140,000 (2024: US$709,140,000, 2023: US$615,000,000) which includes the following banks:

## 12. Loans Payable (Continued)

### 12.1. Senior Credit Agreement (continued)

The Group can choose the interest rate, between the Alternate Base Rate (ABR Loan) $^{7}$ plus the Applicable Margin $^{8}$ and until the replacement of the Benchmark, Eurodollar $^{9}$ and thereafter, SOFR Loan plus the Applicable Margin $^{10}$. Payment of interest with respect to any interest period for a Eurodollar or SOFR borrowing is made at any time on or prior to the term conversion date on the last day of such interest period and thereafter on February 28, May 31, August 31 or November 30 of each year until the maturity date, with respect to any ABR Loan, on February 28, May 31, August 31 and November 30 of each year until the maturity date. The Group reached the term conversion date on July 31, 2025.

During July 2023, the terms of the Senior Credit agreement were amended, which resulted in the replacement of LIBOR-based benchmark rates with Term SOFR Reference Rate, calculated based on adjusted term SOFR with spreads of $0.11448\%$, $0.26161\%$ and $0.42826\%$ for interest periods of one, three and six months, respectively.

### 12.2. HoldCo Credit Agreement

On December 6, 2021, GEGP, entered into a US$175,000,000 credit agreement with GIP CAPS II Tanager Luxco S.À R.L. and Principal Life Insurance Company as lenders and Natixis, New York Branch, as administrative agent, and financial institutions party hereto from time to time, for purpose of financing (i) a portion of project costs, whether through loans or issuance of letters of credit and (ii) certain acquisition costs described in Note 26. The HoldCo Credit Agreement has a maturity date of December 9, 2031. GEGP agrees to pay a commitment fee, which shall accrue at a rate per annum equal to 3.50% on the average daily unused amount of such lenders' commitment during the period from and including the date of this agreement to but excluding the date that such commitment is canceled or expired. The interest rate before the term conversion date is eight and a half percent (8.50%) per annum and after the term conversion date, seven and a half percent (7.50%) per annum. As of December 31, 2025, the interest rate is similar to the market rate; therefore, the fair value of the HoldCo loan is similar to it carrying amount.

Accrued commitment fees related to the HoldCo credit agreement shall be due and payable in arrears on each semiannual date; provided that, prior to the Term Conversion Date, accrued commitment fees shall be paid as PIK commitment fee, and accordingly, the amount of commitment fee due and payable on each semiannual date occurring prior to the Term Conversion Date shall be added to the principal amount of the loans on such semiannual date. The Term Conversion Date occurred on July 31, 2025.

### 12.3. Revolving Credit Line

On January 31, 2025, Gatún entered into a US$20,000,000 revolving credit facility with Global Bank Corporation as lender. The facility has a maturity of twelve months from each disbursement date, with interest payments due on March 20, June 20, September 20, and December 20. The interest rate is based on SOFR plus a margin of 3%, with a minimum annual rate of 5.25%. During 2025 Gatún received disbursements totaling US$7,000,000 and made principal repayments of US$1,500,000 under the revolving credit facility.

## 13. Hedge Accounting Applicable to Senior Credit Agreement

The Group uses derivative financial instruments, essentially interest rate swaps, in order to mitigate the economic effects of interest rate fluctuations to which it is exposed by its activity.

On December 10, 2021, the Group entered into swaps of interest rate agreements with the following banks: Intesa Sanpaolo SPA - New York Branch, Natixis - New York Branch, The Bank of Nova Scotia, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation and Société Générale, with a notional of 85% of the Senior Credit Agreement. The interest fixed rate under those agreements which the Group is committed to pay is 1.856%. The floating rate option for the initial calculation period which the banks were committed to pay until the replacement of the Benchmark was USD-LIBOR 3 month. The payment dates occur every three months on the last day of the month, commencing February 28, 2022.

## 13. Hedge Accounting Applicable to Senior Credit Agreement (Continued)

In June 2023, the terms of the swap agreements were amended with effective date on August 31, to include the replacement of the USD-LIBOR with USD-SOFR-Compound. After that, the Group is committed to pay the fixed rate of 1.636% and the banks are committed to pay USD-SOFR-Compound. The hedge relationship was not discontinued and the accumulated gain in the cash flow hedge reserve is deemed to be based on SOFR.

The use of derivatives for speculative purposes is not permitted within the Group.

No collection risks are expected in relation to the amounts that the financial entities have committed to pay the Group in the future in accordance with the derivatives contracted, since the financial entities with which the derivatives have been contracted are of high solvency.

The valuation of the derivatives contracted by the Group is made mainly by discounting future cash flows. In all cases, the valuation is carried out in accordance with the contractual and market conditions in force at the time of valuation, including credit risk.

The market value of derivatives is determined by directly or indirectly using the information available in the different markets (exchange rate, fixed and variable income, as well as interbank markets and other organized markets).

The variables used to value the derivatives contracted can be classified into 3 categories according to the degree to which their market value is directly observable in the market:

Level 1: those contracted derivatives whose characteristics are identical to those of those listed on an active market.

Level 2: those contracted derivatives whose characteristics are not identical to those of those quoted in an active market, but whose market value can be inferred from prices quoted in one or more active markets.

Level 3: those contracted derivatives that do not belong to levels 1 or 2.

All the variables used to value the derivatives contracted by the Group are level 2.

# Remaining performance obligations

The Group's performance obligations under its PPAs contracts include variable consideration, as the transaction price is determined based on market indices that are subject to significant volatility. The capacity price is indexed monthly to a percentage of the three-month average yield of 30-year U.S. Treasury Bonds, and the energy price is indexed monthly to a percentage of the Henry Hub natural gas spot price.

Given the nature of this variable consideration and the high level of uncertainty associated with future movements in these indices, management has concluded that disclosing a specific quantitative amount of the future performance obligations would not provide reliable or meaningful information, as any estimate could imply a degree of precision that does not exist.

In accordance with IFRS 15, the Group provides qualitative disclosures describing the nature of the variable consideration and the factors that may affect the timing and amount of revenue recognition. Revenue is recognized as the related performance obligations are satisfied, and the transaction price is determined based on the applicable indices at the time the services are rendered.

## Current income tax

Under current tax legislation in the Republic of Panama, the profits of the Group from local operations are subject to income tax.

Income tax is based on the higher of the following computations:

a. The rate of 25% on net taxable income.
b. The rate of 1.17% of gross taxable income (alternative minimum tax).

In certain circumstances, if the application of 1.17% of revenue results in the entity incurring losses for tax reasons, or the effective tax rate is higher than 25%, then the entity may choose to request not to apply minimum tax. In such cases, the Group must file a petition to the Tax Authority, who may authorize the no application for a term of three years.

The income tax by applying the enacted rates to the net profit, is reconciled with the income tax provision presented in the consolidated financial statements, as follows:

## Transfer price

Law No.52 of August 28, 2012, established the transfer pricing regime oriented to regulate tax purposes transactions between related parties, and applicable to the taxpayer to perform operations with related parties that are tax residents of other jurisdictions. The most important aspects of this regulation include:

- Tax payers must submit annually an information return related operations with related parties, within six (6) months following the close of the relevant fiscal period. This obligation applies to transactions from fiscal year 2012.
- Failure to submit the report shall be punishable by a fine equivalent to 1% of the total amount of transactions with related parties.
- Persons required to submit the report referred to in the preceding paragraph, shall maintain a transfer pricing study, which shall contain the information and analysis to assess and document their transactions with related parties, in accordance by Law. The taxpayer must present study only at the request of the Department of Revenue of the Ministry of Economy and Finance within 45 days of your request.

## 26. Commitments

### 26.1. Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)

Power Purchase Agreements. Gatún has entered into the following power purchase agreements for the supply of energy and capacity (collectively, the "PPAs")

i. EDEMET PPA: Power purchase agreement number 20-13 dated June 27, 2013 between Gatún and Empresa de Distribución Eléctrica Metro-Oeste S.A. ("EDEMET"). Under the EDEMET PPA, Gatún agreed to sell energy and capacity to EDEMET from October 1, 2024, to September 30, 2044. The price for the capacity supplied is 18.89 USD/KWh-month and for energy supplied is 0.0880 USD/KWh. The price is indexed monthly based on 10% of the 3-month average of the 30-year U.S. Treasury Bonds (capacity), and 40% of the Henry Hub spot price for natural gas (energy).

ii. EDECHI PPA: Power purchase agreement number 21-13 dated June 27, 2013, between Gatún and Empresa de Distribución Eléctrica Chiriquí S.A. ("EDECHI"). Under the EDECHI PPA, Gatún agreed to sell energy and capacity to EDECHI from October 1, 2024, to September 30, 2044. The price for the capacity supplied is 18.89 USD/KWh-month and for energy supplied is 0.0880 USD/KWh. The price is indexed monthly based on 10% of the 3-month average of the 30-year U.S. Treasury Bonds (capacity), and 40% of the Henry Hub spot price for natural gas (energy).

iii. ENSA PPA: Power purchase agreement number DME-010-13 dated July 3, 2013, between Gatún and Elektra Noreste S.A. ("ENSA"). Under the ENSA PPA, Gatún agreed to sell energy and capacity to ENSA from October 1, 2024, to September 30, 2044. The price for the capacity supplied is 18.89 USD/KWh-month and for energy supplied is 0.0880 USD/KWh. The price is indexed monthly based on 10% of the 3-month average of the 30-year U.S. Treasury Bonds (capacity), and 40% of the Henry Hub spot price for natural gas (energy).

## 27. Contingencies

- On December 30, 2025, a complaint was filed in Virginia District Court, United States of America, by Sinolam LNG Terminal, S.A. and Sinolam Smarter Energy LNG Power Co., Inc. (collectively, “Plaintiffs”) against various defendants, including Group Energy Gas Panama S. de. R.L. (collectively, “Defendants”).

The complaint alleges that the Defendants interfered with the Plaintiffs’ efforts to develop an LNG power projects and seeks recovery of alleged lost profits totaling about $4 billion and other relief from the Defendants. Group Energy Gas Panama S. de R.L. rejects these allegations.

Based on the information currently available, management believes it is premature to reach a conclusion regarding this matter, and it is not currently possible to determine whether it may have an impact on the Company’s financial position, results of operations or cash flows. Accordingly, no amounts have been recognized in these consolidated financial statements.

## 28. Subsequent Events

- In February 2026, the Group entered into a Monetary Settlement Agreement with POSCO E&amp;C Co., Ltd. and POSCO ECO &amp; CHALLENGE Co., Ltd., the contractors responsible for the construction of the Generadora de Gatún plant. This amount had been included in the balances of property, plant and equipment and accounts payable reported in the financial statements as of December 31, 2025.

- In January 2026, the Group entered into three framework agreements for the sale and purchase of energy with Distribuidora de Electricidad del Norte, S.A. (DISNORTE), Excelergy, S.A. de C.V., and GRS Comercializadora, S.A. de C.V.
